chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Anbasa ibn Mus'ab, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who had three wives, so he married two additional women to them in one marriage contract. He slept with one of them, then died. He (peace be upon him) said: 'If he slept with the wife whom he initiated with her name and mentioned her at the time of the marriage contract, then her marriage is valid, and she has inheritance, and upon her is the waiting period. And if he slept with the wife who was named and mentioned after the mention of the first wife, then her marriage is invalid, and there is no inheritance for her, and upon her is the waiting period.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on joint marriage and inheritance if a man dies after sleeping with only one of the wives in a single contract?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* elucidates the Shia juristic principle of *takhassus* (specification) within a joint marriage contract (*'aqd wahid*), where the validity of individual marriages hinges on the specific identification of the bride at the time of contracting. The Imam (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the wife who was explicitly named and the one who was merely included in the general bundle, establishing that only the specifically identified wife acquires full marital rights including inheritance, while the other remains in a state of waiting (*'iddah*) without inheritance. This ruling highlights the importance of precise contractual intent (*niyyah*) in Shia family law, ensuring that ambiguity in multi-wife contracts does not lead to unjust inheritance distribution.
